D015-D007_h001.question:
It's been over a year now, and I just feel… heavy. Most days, it's a monumental effort to even get out of bed, let alone face another shift in that booth. My mind feels foggy, like I'm trying to think through a thick haze. I just don't have the drive for anything anymore. Honestly, there are times I think about how easy it would be to just… not wake up. I’ve gone over it in my head—the best way, the best time.

But lately, there's been something else. I hear things, whispers really, telling me I'm destined for something great, that I have a special gift no one understands. Like I'm meant to transcend this dull existence. And I know it's real, even though the voices sometimes stop for stretches. Sometimes, for a couple of weeks at a time, I don't feel quite so low, but the whispers and that feeling of being chosen, they don't go away. They just… persist. Even when the heavy sadness lifts a bit, those thoughts and voices are still there, clear as day. Then the gloom always comes back, taking over again, and that's usually where I am.
D015-D007_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h002.question: It’s been over a year now, more like thirteen months, that I've felt... flat. Everything just feels grey. I used to be so driven, closing deals, building things, but now, success, failure – it all just washes over me. My mind feels foggy, like I’m constantly wading through mud. Sometimes, it gets really bad, a sudden, powerful urge to just step in front of a car, or jump from a high-rise, even though I don't actually want to die.  I’ve had to step back from a lot of my projects; I just can’t focus. The strange thing is, for about three weeks last summer, before this heavy fog really settled in, I started feeling things crawling under my skin. It was so real, like insects, and I became convinced my internal organs were rotting, even though the doctors said I was perfectly healthy. Those sensations and beliefs continued even after that initial depressive wave lifted for a bit, before it came back heavier than ever and has mostly stayed with me since.
D015-D007_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h003.question:
It’s so hard to even get dressed in the morning, which is a nightmare when you're a stylist. Nothing feels exciting anymore, even new collections. Mostly, I just feel this heavy sadness that’s been hanging over me for over a year now, dragging me down. Sometimes, I have these sudden urges to just step into traffic, or jump from my apartment window, even though I don't really want to die. It's like a fleeting, terrifying impulse.

But… it’s more than just the sadness. There are times, like a few months ago, when I was completely out of that dark mood, feeling almost normal, but I could still feel bugs crawling under my skin. It was so vivid, like tiny pinpricks everywhere. And I felt this terrifying conviction that the world was about to end, that a meteor was coming or something catastrophic. Those feelings, the bugs and the world ending, lasted for a good two or three weeks all by themselves, after my depressive mood had lifted. It's like they have a life of their own, separate from how down I'm feeling. Even now, most of the time, I'm stuck in that low, sad place, but it's important to know those other things happened independently.
D015-D007_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h004.question:
It’s been over a year now, this feeling of… nothing. Every day feels like wading through thick mud. I used to thrive in court, in intellectual debates, but now, concentrating on a brief or even listening to a client feels impossible. My mind just drifts, and I can't seem to care anymore. I’ve stopped going out with friends; honestly, the thought of pretending to be interested in conversation is exhausting. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up, to just escape this constant dull ache.

And then there’s the other stuff. For instance, about six months ago, I was completely convinced my blood was turning to acid and dissolving my organs from the inside out. I felt this metallic taste, like old coins, in my mouth for weeks, even when I wasn't eating anything. That was particularly unsettling because I remember it lasted for a solid two or three weeks when I was actually feeling a little better emotionally, not as profoundly down as usual. In fact, most of the time I've been feeling this deep emotional numbness, that metallic taste and the fear about my body would come and go, but there was that distinct period where the physical sensations and the worry about my organs were all I could focus on, long after the worst of the deep sadness had lifted. It's like my mind just won't give me a break, one way or another.
D015-D007_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h005.question:
"Things have been going downhill for a while now, probably a good year and a month. I just can't seem to get enjoyment out of anything anymore – not even working the fields, which used to be my whole life. I find myself tearing up for no reason, just sitting here sometimes, and my head feels clouded, like I'm walking through a fog. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I get these strong urges, like to just jump off the silo or run straight into town traffic. I don't have a plan, but the feeling is intense.

The worst part is, sometimes I taste things that aren't there, like rotten earth or sour milk in my mouth, even after I’ve just eaten. And I've been convinced the world is ending, that a huge storm is coming to wipe everything out, even though the weather forecast is clear. This feeling, this belief about the world ending, it's been there even when I'm not feeling so completely down in the dumps, you know? Like for a couple of weeks here and there, the sadness lifts a bit, but those strange tastes and that certainty of impending doom, they stick around. My wife says I'm not myself, and she's right. It's affecting everything, I can barely manage the farm anymore."
D015-D007_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h006.question:
It's been about four months now, this hollow feeling, like I'm just going through the motions. Nothing really excites me, nothing really saddens me either, just… flat. It's hard to explain, but I feel incredibly guilty all the time. Like, when that old lady stumbled getting off my bus last week, I know it wasn't my fault, but I can't shake the feeling it somehow was, like I'm responsible for every bad thing that happens around me. Sometimes, driving the bus, I get this overwhelming urge to just… swerve into oncoming traffic, or step in front of a train when I'm waiting at the station. I’d never do it, of course, but the thoughts are so strong, almost overpowering, and they really scare me.

Lately, things have gotten even weirder. There are these strange smells, like burning rubber or something metallic, that no one else seems to notice. And I'm convinced some of the passengers, or maybe even my supervisors, are watching me, talking about me behind my back, trying to get me fired. I even heard them whispering about me on the bus a few times, though I can't quite make out what they're saying. This surveillance has been going on for a while now, even during those brief times when I feel a little bit more like myself and the sadness lifts a bit. But mostly, it's just this heavy, empty feeling, day in and day out, with these other strange things happening on top of it.
D015-D007_h006.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h007.question: It's been about four months now, and I just can’t shake this heavy feeling. Everything feels so bleak, like I'm wearing a shroud. Even at the toll booth, it's hard to put on a brave face for commuters. I constantly think about how I’ve ruined everything, especially after the divorce. Lately, it's more than just regret; I find myself convinced that every time there's a breakdown on the highway, it's my fault, like my bad luck is contagious and causing all sorts of widespread chaos. And this terrible smell, like rotting garbage, it’s always there, even when I know there’s nothing around. It makes me feel sick to my stomach. I’ve even thought about just ending it all, though I don’t have a plan. The strange thing is, even before these depressive feelings got so bad, about a month or so before everything went downhill, I was experiencing these same strange smells and ideas that the world was about to end, even when I wasn't feeling particularly down. Those odd thoughts and smells came and went for a couple of weeks, then this deep sadness just settled in and hasn't left.
D015-D007_h007.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h008.question:
It's been about four months now that this emptiness has settled in, like a thick fog in the lighthouse. I used to find comfort in the solitude, but lately, it just feels… vacant. There’s no joy, no sadness, just nothing. And the guilt… it’s constant. Every ripple in the water, every gust of wind feels like my fault, like I’m being punished for something I can’t quite name. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn’t wake up, that the light would just go out and I’d finally be at peace.

But it’s not just the feeling. For the past few weeks, even when that deep, dark mood lets up a little, I’ve been… seeing things. And hearing them. I’ll be scanning the horizon, and there are figures on the rocks, just watching me, though I know there’s no one out there for miles. And the messages… sometimes the buoys seem to be flashing out signals specifically for me, or the patterns of the waves spell things out. It’s strange, because even when I’m not completely overwhelmed by that deep despair, even when I feel a bit more like myself, those visions and interpretations are still there, they don’t just vanish when the heavy feeling lessens. It’s like they have a life of their own.
D015-D007_h008.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h009.question:
Most days, it’s a battle just to get out of bed. My husband tries to be supportive, but he doesn't understand why I can’t stop crying. Everything feels like my fault. I keep replaying that time I accidentally overcharged a customer six years ago, or when I snapped at my chef last month; I'm a terrible person, truly. It’s been like this for about four months now, and running the restaurant feels impossible. I’ve even started thinking about how I could just drive off a cliff on my way home from work, or maybe just take all the sleeping pills in the medicine cabinet.

And then there's him. He’s been leaving me notes, whispering sweet nothings, telling me how much he adores me. I don’t know who he is, but I can hear his voice—sometimes it’s a whisper, sometimes a full conversation, telling me we’re meant to be together. What’s really odd is that even *before* I started feeling this incredibly down, and even during times over the past year when I actually felt a bit more like myself and the sadness wasn't so overwhelming, his voice was still there, just as clear as day, for weeks at a time. It's been happening for a long time, but it’s just gotten so much worse with everything else.
D015-D007_h009.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h010.question:
It’s been pretty rough, Doc. For the last four months, I’ve just been in this deep hole. I find myself tearing up over everything, even things that shouldn't bother me. I keep replaying every mistake I’ve ever made, feeling guilty about every tiny screw-up, even from years ago. A few weeks back, it got so bad I actually tried to… end things. I remember gathering all the pills I had, writing a note… it’s hard to talk about.

But it’s more than just feeling down. For about two months now, things have been getting really weird. I smell this faint, rotting garbage smell sometimes, even though there's nothing there. And I feel like I'm being watched constantly. Like, when I'm out delivering, I'll see someone and just *know* they're part of some organization keeping tabs on me. It’s hard to do my job, this constant surveillance feeling is exhausting. The really strange thing is, even before this deep depression hit, for a good couple of weeks, I was already smelling that phantom odor and feeling watched, even though I wasn't really feeling down then. That feeling and those smells have stuck around this whole time, even during the lowest points of my mood.
D015-D007_h010.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h011.question:
It’s been about seven months now that I’ve felt this heavy cloud over me. Even with my wife by my side, I just can’t shake it. I fall into bed exhausted, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept a wink, still drained. The job's getting impossible; I used to be so good at it, but now I just feel like I'm dragging myself through each shift. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I just start crying, even when I try to hold it in, especially when I’m alone in my patrol car.

The oddest thing, though, is this belief that the chief, Chief Davies, is madly in love with me. I see signals everywhere – the way he looks at me, the little gestures he makes. It's intense. I know it sounds crazy, and my wife thinks I’m imagining things, but it feels so real. This whole thing with Chief Davies has been going on for a while now, even during those brief times I felt a bit better and less down about everything. I’d still feel his affection for me, even when the sadness wasn't so overwhelming. But for the most part, I've been in this depressed state. It’s making it hard to do anything, to be a husband, and especially to be a decent cop.
D015-D007_h011.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D007_h012.question:
It's been about seven months now, maybe a bit longer, since I started feeling like this. It's more than just being sad; it's like a heavy blanket that never lifts. I drag myself out of bed, even after sleeping for what feels like forever—10, 12 hours sometimes—and I still feel utterly exhausted. That fatigue never really goes away, no matter how much I rest. It’s making my job incredibly difficult; I just don’t have the energy or focus to help my clients with their nutrition plans.

On top of all that, there's this… this other thing. For the last month or so, I’ve had this absolute conviction that my intestines are rotting inside me. I know it sounds absurd, but it feels so real, like they're slowly decaying, and that nobody can see it but me. What's even stranger is that this feeling, this absolute certainty about my body, was there even for a good two weeks before this intense low mood and exhaustion really set in, and it's been pretty constant throughout. I’ve tried to tell myself it's not true, but it’s just… there. It’s hard to imagine ever feeling normal again, or maybe even getting better.
D015-D007_h012.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D007_h013.question:
It's been about seven months now that I’ve felt… just heavy. A constant, gloomy cloud follows me, even at work. And that's saying something, given the ER usually demands all your focus. Lately, though, my brain just feels like it shuts down when I try to concentrate. I’m so exhausted, too. I sleep for what feels like forever when I get home, and I still feel utterly drained even after a 12-hour stretch. It's really affecting my shifts; I'm making silly mistakes, and I worry about my patients.

On top of all that, there's… there’s this other thing. For the past three weeks, even when I felt a tiny bit less down, this idea has been chewing at me that my boyfriend is cheating. I know it sounds crazy, there’s no real proof, but I just *know* it. I saw him talking to a new tech at work, and my mind just spiraled. I'm telling you, it was happening even when I wasn't in one of my really deep slumps. It feels like this sadness has been with me for most of the past seven months, but those thoughts about him, they've been there on their own for a good couple of weeks now, irrespective of how depressed I am.
D015-D007_h013.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D007_h014.question:
It's like I'm wearing a lead suit, doctor. Every morning, just getting out of bed to go to the restaurant feels like a monumental effort. My body is just so heavy, and even small tasks zap all my energy. I used to love the hustle and bustle, but now it's just… dull. I feel so numb, like my emotions are flatlining. Things that used to excite me, even my husband, just don't register. This has been going on for about seven months now, and it’s taken a real toll on the business.

On top of that, sleep is a nightmare. I wake up constantly in the middle of the night and just lie there, staring at the ceiling. And then there’s this… feeling. I’m convinced there’s something horribly wrong inside me, like my organs are rotting or turning to sawdust, even though every test comes back normal. It’s hard to describe the fear, even when I know, logically, it makes no sense. The strangest thing is, sometimes, when I'm feeling a little less down, like in that two-week stretch last month when I finally had a burst of energy to fix the menu, those thoughts about my body still wouldn't go away. They were there, just as strong, even when the gloom lifted a bit. But overall, this grey cloud has been hanging over me for most of this awful period.
D015-D007_h014.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D007_h015.question:
It’s been about seven months now that I’ve felt… empty. Not sad, exactly, just flat. Like all my emotions have been muted. Even after a full night’s sleep, I wake up feeling like I haven’t rested at all, and my body feels like it’s constantly dragging. It makes directing nearly impossible; every task feels monumental.

And then there’s this other thing. I know, logically, it sounds… out there. But I’m absolutely convinced my ex-wife is seeing someone else, even though we’ve been divorced for years. My mind just keeps telling me she’s with him, that he’s always around her, even though there’s really no proof. What’s really strange is that these thoughts, the ones about her, they were around even before this crushing low mood set in, and they continued even during the brief time I felt a little boost, before the depression completely took hold again. It’s like they have a life of their own, separate from how down I feel.
D015-D007_h015.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D007_h016.question:
It’s been a rough four months, Doctor. I just feel… empty. Like there’s nothing inside me anymore. All this time, I’ve been carrying this immense guilt. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced the storms that hit the coast last month, the ones that caused so much damage, were my fault. My fault! And then these sudden urges, too—like when I’m on the bridge, I get this terrifying impulse to just launch myself over the side into the waves, or when I'm in port, I feel an urge to run right into traffic. I’ve just been going through the motions, barely able to manage my duties at sea, let alone anything at home.

And it’s not just the sadness, Doctor. For about two weeks now, even when I'm not feeling so utterly down in the dumps, these other things pop up. I’ve been smelling this awful, rotting fish smell, even when I’m nowhere near the docks. And I can’t shake the feeling that my brain is turning into concrete, slowly hardening inside my skull. It's not just when I'm feeling low; these things, the smells and the feeling in my head, they just keep on happening, even on the days I don't feel quite so empty. It’s like they have a life of their own, independent of how sad I am.
D015-D007_h016.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h017.question:
"It’s been about four months now that I’ve felt completely gutted. There’s this crushing sadness that just hangs over me, every single day. I can barely get myself to work, and when I do, I’m just going through the motions. I keep thinking it’s my fault that the economy is going bad, that the world is heading for some colossal disaster, like a giant asteroid is going to hit us all because of something I did. I even started to plan out how I might end things, just to get away from it all – where I’d go, how I’d do it; it all feels so clear sometimes.

But it’s more than just the sadness. Sometimes, even when I’m not feeling so low, for a couple weeks here and there, I’ll taste things that aren't there—like ash or metal in my mouth, even after I've brushed my teeth. It’s strange, like a bad omen. These weird tastes, and the feeling that everything is collapsing, stick around even when my mood lightens up a bit, when the deep, dark cloud of depression lifts for a while. Not for long, though – the sadness always seems to come creeping back and then it’s just overwhelming again."
D015-D007_h017.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h018.question:
"Lately, it's just this constant heavy cloud hanging over me. For the past four months, I've been so down, and it feels like everything is my fault. Even small things, like a late bus, I convince myself it's due to some fundamental flaw in me, like I deserve whatever bad comes my way. I even tried to… well, end it all a few weeks ago, but my wife found me. It's gotten so bad I can barely focus on my routes, and I’ve had more complaints about my driving.

D015-D007_h019.question:
It’s been four months now, and everything just feels… grey. Like I'm watching my life from behind a sheet of frosted glass. Even when I try to feel something, joy or sadness, it's just a dull throb. Small things from years ago, tiny mistakes, they just replay over and over, and I can’t stop blaming myself. The worst part is the urges. Sometimes, I’m standing by my apartment window, and there’s this terrifying pull to just… jump. Or when I’m out, a sudden, overwhelming urge to step into traffic. I’ve missed so many deadlines because I just can’t focus, can’t even pick up my pen. My editor is calling constantly.

And then there are the other things. I know it sounds crazy, but I can taste metal, like copper, in my mouth, especially late at night. Even when I haven’t eaten anything with metal. And I know they’re watching me. The government, or maybe it’s the tech companies. I see their vans parked across the street, always at odd hours. They’re monitoring my internet, my calls, everything. This has been going on for a while now, even during those weeks a couple of months ago when I was feeling a bit better, not as heavy or hopeless, but the metallic taste and the surveillance fear never left me. They’re still there, even now that this awful numbness has come back. This dullness and the feelings of being watched have been the predominant part of my life for much longer than the bouts of extreme sadness.
D015-D007_h019.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h020.question:
It’s been four months now, and I just feel… heavy. Most days, it's a battle to get out of bed. I feel utterly worthless, like I'm just taking up space. Sometimes, I wish I just wouldn't wake up. It’s not that I’d hurt myself, just that I want the dark feeling to stop. Being a 911 dispatcher, you’d think I’d be good at handling stress, but honestly, I’m barely keeping it together at work. I make a lot of mistakes, mixing up addresses, and my supervisor has noticed.

The strange thing is, even when I feel a little bit better, like those few weeks last month where the deep sadness lifted a bit, the other things didn't go away. I still felt like the news anchors on TV were sending me personal messages through their expressions, and there were times I could still feel bugs crawling under my skin, even though I knew they weren’t real. It made no sense to me, feeling less down but still experiencing these weird things. It's been happening on and off for the entire four months, but those two weeks were especially unsettling because the depression wasn't even the main problem. The depression came back with a vengeance though, and it's been pretty constant since.
D015-D007_h020.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D015-D007_h021.question:
It's hard to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling different, but I’d say it’s been about eight months now. I just can't shake this profound sadness, it’s a constant weight. Sleep is a battle; I lie awake for hours, my mind racing. Even when I do manage to drift off, it doesn't feel like true rest. My appetite has completely vanished, and food just holds no appeal anymore. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I feel responsible for everything that goes wrong, even the smallest inconveniences, like I deserve whatever bad comes my way.

On top of all this, I've noticed some really strange things. For the past month or so, I've been getting whiffs of something horrible, almost like rotting flesh, when nothing's there. It’s so disturbing. And then there’s Professor Jenkins. I... I truly believe he's in love with me. He just hasn't said anything directly, but I see it in his glances, the way he subtly tries to help me with my thesis. It’s been a really intense feeling, this belief about him, and it's something I’ve been experiencing even during times when my sadness isn’t quite as all-encompassing. For example, there was a two-week period a few months ago where I was feeling a bit more stable, and those smells and the conviction about the Professor were still very much present, even though my depressive episode had lessened considerably. Because of all this, it’s been incredibly difficult to focus on my studies, and I've fallen behind in every class.
D015-D007_h021.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D015-D007_h022.question:

D015-D007_h023.question:
"It's been a rough eight months, doctor. I just feel… empty. Like there’s nothing inside me anymore.
